motivation: Community-buffering v1 showed that most exact meter marks losing Thalassia remained occupied by another seagrass, but target occupancy alone cannot distinguish persistence of pre-existing mixed-species patches from new colonization after focal loss.

source.source_taxonomy: present Alismatales; focal species Thalassia testudinum

primary_population.transition: same stable point observed in consecutive years; source-year Thalassia present; target-year Thalassia absent
primary_population.rationale: The prior Lower-specific exact-point endpoint was non-estimable under frozen minima, so this is a new all-bay ecological question rather than a lowered Lower-Tampa threshold.

H3a_source_mixture_insurance.statement: After exact-point Thalassia loss, points where another seagrass already co-occurred with Thalassia in the source year are more likely to remain seagrass-occupied than source points containing Thalassia alone.
H3a_source_mixture_insurance.exposure: source_mixed = source-year alternative_species nonempty while Thalassia present
H3a_source_mixture_insurance.outcome: target_any_seagrass_present; because target Thalassia is absent, this equals target alternative-seagrass occupancy
H3a_source_mixture_insurance.estimator: node-cluster bootstrap difference in target occupancy fraction: source mixed minus source Thalassia-only
H3a_source_mixture_insurance.support_rule: bootstrap 95% interval for mixed-minus-Thalassia-only occupancy difference entirely above zero

H3b_persistence_not_colonization.statement: Among Thalassia-loss points that remain occupied by another seagrass, the majority retain at least one alternative species that was already co-occurring in the source year rather than being occupied exclusively by newly appearing alternative species.
H3b_persistence_not_colonization.retained_species: intersection of source and target alternative-species sets is nonempty
H3b_persistence_not_colonization.support_rule: bootstrap 95% lower bound for retained-species fraction > 0.5

descriptive_only: species identity of retained versus newly appearing alternatives
Lower Tampa Bay subset; it cannot replace pooled primary tests if the pooled tests fail
claim_boundary: A positive source-mixture association would be consistent with community insurance but would not identify facilitation; mixed points may share persistent habitat quality.
Retained alternative species after focal loss indicates persistence of co-occurring community members, not functional equivalence to Thalassia.
Newly appearing alternative species are observational colonization/appearance events and do not establish competitive replacement.
Do not change the pooled geography, target years, transition definition, bootstrap unit, or support thresholds after opening source-year co-occurrence results.
